title: Apple researchers introduce SCLATE for training and evaluating agentic models
excerpt: The new execution substrate compresses month-long scenarios into hours by using a hybrid simulated clock to manage events.
bodyHtml:
Apple researchers announced SCLATE on September 30, 2026, as an execution substrate designed for training and evaluating continual-learning agents. These agents are systems of models, harnesses, and memory that operate over long multi-session horizons.

SCLATE functions as an open event scheduler where benchmarks and agents add their events through an adapter. A hybrid simulated clock runs these events on a shared timeline, allowing the system to skip idle gaps and compress a month-long scenario into hours. The platform also acts as a rollout engine that records tokens and log probabilities of model calls through an in-container proxy.

Researchers ported seven benchmarks to the platform and compared ten unmodified harness and memory configurations. The comparison shows that an added memory system does not reliably beat the harness's native memory and that models differ widely in how they use the same harness and memory. When the team used Qwen3.5-4B through unmodified harnesses and memory systems, the model read 6.8× fewer file lines with a 16.7-point higher SWE-bench Verified pass rate, while its held-out MetaClaw accuracy rose by up to 11.8 points.
